lesson.text: Remember? A sentence has a subject and a verb, and it makes sense on its own: The cat slept.
A simple sentence has one idea: "The cat slept." A compound sentence joins two ideas with and, but, or or so: "The cat slept, and the dog played."
Choose the joining word by its meaning. And adds more. But shows a difference: "I was tired, but I kept going." So shows a result: "It was cold, so I wore a hat."
A complex sentence joins ideas with because, when, if, while, before or after: "We went inside because it rained." "When the bell rang, we lined up."
Because gives a reason. When tells the time. If tells what must happen first: "If it snows, we will build a snowman."
Mix short and long sentences, and choose the joining word that says exactly what you mean. Your writing will flow like a story told aloud.
Try it in the world: write a sign for your house that joins two ideas: "It was cold, so we built a fire." Which joining word did you choose, and why? Next: speech marks and apostrophes.

exercises.prompt: Choose the joining word: "I like apples ___ pears."
exercises.explain: And adds more: I like apples and pears.

exercises.hint: A simple sentence has one idea.
choices: The cat slept, and the dog played.
The cat slept because it was tired.
exercises.explain: "The cat slept." has just one idea.

exercises.prompt: Choose the joining word: "I was tired, ___ I kept going."
exercises.explain: But shows a difference: tired, but still going.

exercises.prompt: Choose the joining word: "It was cold, ___ I wore a hat."
exercises.hint: Wearing a hat was the result.
exercises.explain: So shows a result: it was cold, so I wore a hat.

exercises.prompt: Choose the joining word: "We went inside ___ it rained."
exercises.explain: Because gives the reason: we went inside because it rained.

exercises.hint: It joins two ideas with and, but, or or so.
exercises.explain: Two ideas joined with and: a compound sentence.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence about the bell.
exercises.hint: Start with the word with a capital letter.
exercises.explain: When the bell rang, we lined up.

exercises.prompt: Choose the joining word: "___ it snows, we will build a snowman."
exercises.hint: It tells what must happen first.
exercises.explain: If it snows, we will build a snowman.

exercises.prompt: Which joins these best? "The river was deep. We used the bridge."
exercises.hint: Why did we use the bridge?
choices: The river was deep, so we used the bridge.
The river was deep, but we used the bridge.
The river was deep or we used the bridge.
exercises.explain: The deep river is why we used the bridge: so shows the result.

exercises.prompt: Choose the joining word: "Wash your hands ___ you eat."
exercises.explain: Wash your hands before you eat.

exercises.hint: Look for because, when, if, while, before or after.
choices: We stayed in because it was stormy.
We stayed in, and we read.
exercises.explain: "Because it was stormy" gives a reason: a complex sentence.

exercises.prompt: Choose the joining word: "Bram read a book ___ he waited for the bus."
exercises.hint: Both things happened at the same time.
exercises.explain: While means at the same time.

exercises.prompt: "I wanted to play, but it was raining." uses but to show a difference.
exercises.hint: Wanting to play and rain do not match.
exercises.explain: True: but shows that the second idea is different from the first.

exercises.prompt: Match each joining word to its job.
exercises.hint: Try each one in a sentence about going inside, the bell, or snow.
exercises.explain: Because gives a reason, when tells the time, and if tells what must happen first.

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences: compound or complex?
items: The cat slept, and the dog played.
We went in because it rained.
It was cold, so I wore a hat.
When the bell rang, we lined up.
exercises.hint: Compound sentences join with and, but, or or so.
exercises.explain: And and so make compound sentences; because and when make complex ones.

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences by what the joining word does.
items: I was tired, but I kept going.
It was cold, so I wore a hat.
It is small, but it is strong.
It rained, so we stayed in.
exercises.hint: And adds more, but shows a difference, so shows a result.
exercises.explain: And adds more: apples and pears, Pip and Nell. But shows a difference: tired but going, small but strong. So shows a result: a hat for the cold, staying in for the rain.

exercises.prompt: Build a sentence that starts with its reason.
exercises.hint: Start with the joining word that gives a reason. A comma ends the reason part.
exercises.explain: Because it was dark, we lit a lamp. The because part comes first, so a comma goes after it, then the main idea.
